items.title: Positive Breakout: These 7 stocks cross above their 200 DMAs
items.description: In the Nifty500 pack, seven stocks' closing prices crossed above their 200-day moving averages (DMA) on October 28, 2026, according to StockEdge's technical scan data. The 200-day moving average (DMA) is used by traders as a key indicator for determining the overall trend of a stock. As long as a stock's price remains above its 200-day moving average on the daily timeframe, it is generally interpreted as being in an overall uptrend.

items.title: Jio listing propels Reliance past Tata Group as India's biggest conglomerate
items.description: The listing of Jio Platforms has significantly impacted India's corporate rankings, with Reliance Industries regaining the top position. Reliance's market capitalisation rose to approximately ₹30.26 lakh crore, overtaking the Tata Group. Jio's shares closed at ₹1,417.35, reflecting a 26.66% premium over the issue price. This transition highlights the challenges faced by other conglomerates, such as the Tata Group and Mahindra Group.

items.title: Jio Platforms breaks into global top 5 telcos after listing
items.description: Jio Platforms made its public listing in India, achieving a market cap of $137.3 billion. This valuation positions it as the fifth-largest telecom company worldwide, surpassing Deutsche Telekom. Global competitors like China Mobile and Verizon continue to lead in market capitalization. Jio's valuation reflects its advanced 4G and 5G networks, which differ from legacy infrastructures of global giants.

items.title: Jio Platforms draws bullish bets, analysts see up to 28% upside
items.description: Four brokerages have begun coverage on Jio Platforms just before its upcoming listing with favorable ratings. Nomura, Motilal Oswal Securities, and Elara Capital issued 'Buy' ratings indicating significant upside potential. Dolat Capital provided an 'Accumulate' rating with a higher target price suggesting a 28% increase. Analysts believe Jio Platforms may influence tariffs in the telecom industry substantially.

items.title: MSCI puts Polycab exit on hold amid insolvency case uncertainty
items.description: MSCI has decided to delay the removal of Polycab India from its indices amid insolvency uncertainty. The company was placed on the Insolvency Resolution Process board on October 7. However, the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal stayed the company’s admission to the insolvency process on October 9. MSCI continues to monitor the status of Polycab India and any related orders from the NCLAT.

items.title: Jio Platforms shares surge 21% on debut, overtake Airtel in market cap
items.description: Jio Platforms made a remarkable entrance in the stock market, soaring 21.4% above its IPO price on the first day of trading. Closing at ₹1,417.35, the stock surpassed Bharti Airtel in market capitalization. With a staggering 22 times oversubscription, the IPO attracted considerable institutional backing. At the launch event, executive director Anant Ambani recognized the invaluable support from millions of subscribers.

items.title: Stocks in news: Jio Platforms, RIL, Hero MotoCorp, Meesho, TVS Motor, Vedanta Aluminium and Suzlon Energy
items.description: Indian equities ended lower on Wednesday, primarily driven by selling in heavyweight stocks. Information technology and oil and gas shares experienced significant declines, falling more than 2%. The Nifty 50 index settled at 22,699, down 51 points, indicating ongoing resistance at 22,800. Several companies, including Jio Platforms and Hero MotoCorp, reported their quarterly earnings that impacted market sentiment.

items.title: D-Street poised for positive start as GIFT Nifty signals gains
items.description: Benchmark Nifty experienced a marginal decline after recovering from a significant low during the trading session. Analysts believe Indian equities may remain range-bound. The rupee weakened against the US dollar due to rising crude oil prices and a strengthening dollar. Foreign portfolio investors were net buyers on Wednesday, with significant purchases noted.

items.title: Sensex, Nifty fall as IT stocks slide, rising oil prices weigh
items.description: Indian equity markets took a hit on Wednesday, primarily due to declines in the IT sector and escalating crude oil prices. Both the Sensex and Nifty closed lower, showcasing investors' cautious mood amidst significant intraday drops. Key downturns were influenced by Reliance Industries along with various IT stocks, but the auto sector and select banking stocks sparked some buying activities that alleviated part of the losses.

items.title: Sebi to review FPI rules, align with global norms
items.description: The Securities and Exchange Board of India is set to release a consultation paper aimed at refining compliance requirements for foreign portfolio investors. Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey highlighted the progress in the onboarding of international funds while pointing out the heavy compliance burden in India. Sebi is also considering the possibility of self-listing for stock exchanges despite the challenges that may arise.

items.title: Stock Radar: RIL showing signs of recovery; forms triple bottom formation on weekly charts – time to buy?
items.description: Reliance Industries Ltd has found support around the 1,100 level, indicating a possible bounce back. Medium-term traders are advised to consider buying the stock for targets above 1,300 levels. The stock recently closed at Rs 1,200, having experienced a decline over the past months. Analysts note a triple-bottom pattern that could signal easing selling pressure. Investors should assess technical indicators before making trading decisions.

items.title: Jio Platforms lists on NSE as 3,138th company, making Ambani family proud with a 21.36% surge
items.description: Jio Platforms became the 3,138th company to list on the NSE after a significant public offering. The listing resulted in a notable 21.36% increase, making Jio the second most valuable Indian company. Mukesh Ambani expressed strong emotions as he witnessed his children outline their vision for the future. Following the listing ceremony, the family visited a temple and celebrated with a drone show.

items.title: ACME Solar shares rally 5% after Q2 profit jumps over 100%, signs 400MV agreement with NTPC
items.description: ACME Solar shares rose 5% after its Q2 FY27 profit surged 133.5% to ₹269 crore and revenue climbed 67.5% to ₹1,007 crore. The rally was also supported by its subsidiary signing a 25-year power purchase agreement with NTPC for a 400 MW renewable energy project.

items.title: Jio Platforms is becoming more than a telecom company: Dolat Capital
items.description: Jio Platforms is poised to evolve beyond telecom as tariff hikes, 5G monetisation, home broadband and enterprise digital services drive its next growth phase, according to Dolat Capital. The brokerage initiated coverage with an Accumulate rating and a target price of Rs 1,435, citing strong growth prospects and rising free cash flow.

items.title: Technical picks for Diwali! 10 stocks PL Capital is bullish on this festive season. See full list
items.description: Samvat 2082 proved challenging for Indian equities, marked by heightened volatility, intermittent recoveries and a significant correction in benchmark indices. Over the next 12 months, the sustainability and breadth of corporate earnings growth are likely to be the key drivers of equity market returns. Here are 10 stocks that look strong on charts.

items.title: Michael Burry says Anthropic IPO papers show AI industry is 'catastrophically vulnerable'. What the 'Big Short' investor sees
items.description: Investor Michael Burry warned that Anthropic’s planned IPO exposes serious vulnerabilities in the AI industry, citing massive infrastructure commitments, slowing growth and mounting costs. The investor, known for predicting the 2008 financial crisis, believes disappointing AI revenues could trigger a significant market correction and capital losses.

items.title: HUL shares rise 3% after Q2 results. Jefferies, Nomura cut target price but forecast 29% upside potential
items.description: Hindustan Unilever shares rose on Thursday after the FMCG major reported a 4% year-on-year increase in Q2 FY27 net profit to Rs 2,790 crore and 15% revenue growth to Rs 18,226 crore. Jefferies, Nomura and JM Financial cut their target prices but continue to see upside potential of up to 29%.

items.title: Adani group stocks jump up to 3%, add Rs 23,000 crore to total m-cap. What’s behind the surge?
items.description: Adani Group stocks rose on Thursday, adding Rs 23,000 crore to their combined market capitalisation, as Q2 results and bullish brokerage calls lifted sentiment. Adani Power reported a 134% jump in net profit, while Jefferies raised its target price for Adani Ports and sees significant upside in Adani Enterprises.

items.title: Jefferies initiates coverage on NSE with ‘Buy’; here’s why it sees fresh growth potential
items.description: Jefferies has initiated coverage on NSE with a ‘Buy’ rating and a target price of Rs 2,085, indicating over 17% upside. The brokerage expects structural growth, market leadership, diversification and new businesses to drive a 15% revenue CAGR over FY27–29 and support margin expansion.

items.title: City Union Bank shares rally 7% after Q2 net profit grows 27% YoY to Rs 416 Crore
items.description: City Union Bank shares rose sharply on Thursday after the lender reported a 27% year-on-year rise in Q2 FY27 net profit to Rs 416 crore. Net interest income grew 31%, while asset quality improved, with gross NPAs falling to 1.44%. Deposits and advances also recorded strong growth during the quarter.

items.title: Why is market rising today? Sensex jumps 700 points, Nifty nears 22,900. 6 key factors behind Rs 3 lakh crore gains
items.description: On Thursday, the Indian stock market saw significant upward movement, propelled by the Federal Reserve's decision to maintain steady interest rates. The Sensex climbed by over 700 points, surpassing the 73,956 mark, while Nifty 50 gained nearly 200 points, approaching 22,900. Broader indices like Nifty Smallcap 100 and Nifty Midcap 100 also witnessed increases of up to 0.6%. Traders should brace for potential fluctuations as expiry day approaches.

items.title: Sensex jumps over 500 points, Nifty above 22,850 after Fed keeps rates unchanged. What lies ahead?
items.description: Following the Federal Reserve's recent decision, the Indian stock market surged, with Sensex rising by over 500 points and Nifty up by more than 150 points. Adani Ports and Power Grid were among the top gainers, while Trent faced a downturn. The breadth of the market remained positive, as advances outnumbered declines on the NSE. Analysts, however, highlighted potential global economic issues that could pose challenges for India.

items.title: Jupiter Wagons shares rally 8% on Rs 1,140 crore Railway Board order
items.description: Jupiter Wagons shares rallied over 8% after securing a Rs 1,140 crore Railway Board order for 2,583 wagons. The company expects additional order inflows of around Rs 2,000 crore in Q4 FY27, supported by government and private-sector demand. Despite the gains, the stock has fallen 25% in three months and trades below seven of its eight simple moving averages.

items.title: CarTrade Tech shares tank over 6% after Q2 results, but Nomura raises target price to Rs 3,377. Here’s why
items.description: CarTrade Tech shares fell 6.5% after Q2FY27 net profit rose 3% year-on-year to Rs 66 crore, while revenue increased 10% to Rs 213 crore. Nomura raised its target price to Rs 3,377 from Rs 3,340, citing growth potential in OLX India, improving consumer business prospects and operating leverage, despite trimming revenue estimates by around 3%.

items.title: Hyundai Motor shares jump 6% even as Q2 net profit declines 24% YoY. Why Nomura, other brokerages remain bullish?
items.description: Hyundai Motor India shares rose despite a sharp decline in Q2 FY27 profit as rising commodity costs squeezed margins. Nomura and Motilal Oswal retained their Buy ratings, citing new model launches, export growth and potential margin recovery.

items.title: Potential LTCG tax cut could revive FIIs’ India bet, says Jefferies: Which stocks may benefit most?
items.description: Jefferies sees a potential long-term capital gains tax (LTCG) cut as a possible trigger for foreign investors to return to Indian equities after record outflows. Banks, Reliance Industries, utilities and real estate stocks could be the biggest beneficiaries. Here’s where foreign investors are positioned and what a tax cut could mean.

items.title: Nifty’s early comeback signal: Why largecaps are holding up as broader market slides
items.description: India’s equity market divergence suggests largecaps may be regaining leadership as mid- and smallcaps remain under pressure. The Nifty has recovered to broadly flat returns in October, while midcap and smallcap indices have declined. More reasonable valuations, earnings resilience, liquidity and institutional preference are supporting largecaps, though elevated crude prices, macroeconomic uncertainty and earnings concerns continue to cloud the broader market outlook.

items.title: Adani Ports shares rise 3% after Q2 results. Why did Jefferies and Nomura raise target prices?
items.description: Adani Ports shares rose after the company reported strong Q2 FY27 earnings and raised its full-year guidance. Jefferies and Nomura increased their target prices, citing robust international port performance, higher earnings estimates and long-term growth prospects.

items.title: Market Trading Guide: Eternal among 2 stocks to buy for Friday for healthy returns
items.description: Indian stocks rallied after the US Federal Reserve held rates steady, easing crude prices and renewed institutional buying lifted sentiment. Technical analysts identified Adani Ports and Eternal as potential Friday trading opportunities, citing bullish momentum, breakout levels and defined targets.

items.title: Two Trades for Today: A realty major for a 5.15% rise, a mid-cap manufacturing solutions provider’s stock for a gain of 7%
items.description: Our technical analysts identify select stocks every trading day that may gain momentum even in volatile markets. Here are the technical calls for today.

items.title: Shukra Medtech, Laurus Labs among 4 healthcare stocks to hit 52-week highs and rally up to 26% in a month
items.description: On Thursday, the benchmark Sensex surged 905 points to close at 74,151. Amid the market rally, four stocks from the BSE Healthcare index touched fresh 52-week highs, reaching their highest levels in the past year. A 52-week high marks the highest price at which a stock has traded over the preceding 12 months and may reflect increased market activity and investor interest.

items.title: Market wrap:  Adani Ports SEZ, Adani Ent, Trent, Maruti Suzuki top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Thursday
items.description: Indian equities rallied on Thursday, with the Sensex rising 905 points and the Nifty gaining 238 points as easing crude oil prices, the US Federal Reserve’s rate decision and institutional buying lifted sentiment. Adani Ports SEZ and Adani Enterprises led Nifty gainers, while Trent and Maruti Suzuki were among the top losers.

items.title: Weekly Top Picks: These stocks scored 10 on 10 on Stock Reports Plus
items.description: Stock Reports Plus, powered by Refinitiv, undertakes detailed company analysis for 4,000+ listed stocks. In addition to detailed company analyses, the report also collates analysts’ forecasts and trend analysis for each component. An average score in Stock Reports Plus is calculated by undertaking quantitative analysis of five key investment tools – earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum.

items.title: For investors with ability to look past the current bearish narrative: 5 large-cap stocks with upside potential of up to 34%
items.description: One stock not falling on bad news does not mean the worst is over for the whole market. It may mean only that the bears have, for now, taken out of that one stock all that they wanted to. The broader pressure can still come back. So this is a small positive, and it should be considered just that, and nothing more.

items.title: 10 defence stocks rally up to 500% in FY27 so far; 5 turn multibaggers
items.description: While the Nifty 50 has gained just around 2% so far in FY27, the Nifty India Defence index has surged nearly 22%, significantly outperforming the benchmark. The rally has been broad-based, with most defence stocks delivering returns of over 25%. We take a look at the top 10 performers, which have rallied between 40% and 500%, including five multibagger stocks. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: Tata Power, JSW Energy, Torrent Power: Ambit sees buying opportunity in power stocks after valuation reset
items.description: Ambit Capital sees the recent correction in power stocks as a re-entry opportunity, favouring Tata Power, JSW Energy and Torrent Power. Rising electricity demand, fresh capacity contracting and limited PPA visibility could drive the sector’s next growth phase.

items.title: Bajaj Electricals exec chairman Shekhar Bajaj to become non-executive board member from January
items.description: Bajaj Electricals executive chairman Shekhar Bajaj will step down from his current role by the end of 2026 after leading the company for four decades. He will transition to a non-executive board position from January 1, 2027, subject to shareholder approval. The move is part of the company’s shift towards a professionally managed, board-led governance model, it said.

items.title: Pine Labs shares jump 7% as Q2 net profit soars 543% YoY to Rs 39 crore
items.description: Pine Labs shares rose sharply on Thursday after the fintech company reported a 543% year-on-year jump in Q2 FY27 net profit to Rs 38.6 crore. Revenue rose 24% to Rs 806.2 crore, while EBITDA increased 67.3%. Growth in payments, UPI transactions and international markets supported performance as the company expands into AI-led commerce.

items.title: These large-, mid- and small-cap stocks can give more than 20% return in 1 year, according to analysts
items.description: Here’s one thing that is worth clarifying, because it is in the headlines. Large global technology companies have been announcing heavy spending on AI, and there has been some correction in those stocks because of it. It is natural to worry that this will spill over into the Indian market. It most likely will not.

items.title: Sagility block deal: Promoter Sagility BV likely to sell 12% stake for Rs 2,377 crore
items.description: Sagility promoter Sagility B.V. is reportedly planning a 12% stake sale worth ₹2,377 crore through a block deal. The healthcare IT services firm posted 22.5% revenue growth and 8.1% adjusted profit growth in Q2 FY27.

items.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Friday
items.description: Indian equities rallied over 1% on Thursday as the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady, crude prices eased and institutional buying strengthened sentiment. Sensex gained 905 points, while Nifty rose 238 points, adding nearly ₹5 lakh crore in market value.
